subject: Session bucket rounding & pilot credit details

Subject: Session bucket rounding & pilot credit details

Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation VentureByte is trying to validate cost predictability for a multi-user pilot (chat + embedding lookups). Before Marissa and I get to contract language, I wanted to clarify how we bill for short-lived sessions and streaming responses so you have concrete examples to share with procurement. High level:

- We bill per token consumed (prompt + generated), with a session-level aggregation window and a small rounding quantum for sessions under a threshold.
- Questions you raised: whether streaming increments are billed differently, whether prefix/KV cache hits are chargeable, and how minimum buckets/credits would apply during the pilot.

Attached: pilot_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW draft — pricing callout on p2).

Quick answers up front (we'll expand below):
1) Streaming: tokens emitted during a stream are billed the same as non-streamed tokens; we increment in quantums.
2) Cache: KV/prefix served from cache still counts toward billing if the model must re-materialize the token; pure cache hits (no model compute) are not charged.
3) Pilot credit: we can offer a 10% pilot credit applied to the first monthly invoice plus a one-time 5k token credit to offset rounding for low-volume users.

I'll follow up with worked examples and a suggested clause for the SOW. If you want a different credit structure (e.g., fixed dollar credit vs token credit), let me know and we can adjust.

Thanks —
Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Connor —

Thanks for the summary and the quick answers. A couple of clarifying items from procurement/engineering:

1) Examples: can you show how billing looks for (a) a 250-token prompt with a 150-token response (one-off), (b) a 12-message chat session for an individual agent where total tokens are 1,120, and (c) an embedding-only call with a 64-token input for 10k records per day? We want to see how rounding and minimums move cost across those shapes.
2) Streaming: does the rounding quantum apply per chunk emitted or at session-finalization? If a stream emits 7 chunks of 20 tokens, are we rounded 7x?
3) Cache: you mentioned "pure cache hits not charged" — can you define what counts as a pure hit vs a cached prefix that still triggers compute? Procurement is sensitive to any ambiguity.

Also: if we accept an initial pilot with the 10% invoice credit, would you be open to a prorated committed minimum for month 2 if usage ramps? Procurement prefers an explicit floor discussion now.

Appreciate the worked examples.
Alex
Head of Integrations
VentureByte
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Session bucket rounding & pilot credit details

Connor / Karthik —

Looping you both in with procurement asks. My suggestion for negotiation posture: offer the 10% invoice credit + a one-time 5k token credit (as Connor suggested) and be explicit that rounding is applied at the session level using a 100-token quantum for sessions under 2k tokens. Rationale: keeps pilot economics simple and small customers won't get hit by micro-charges, while we avoid having to meter to the token.

Proposed language for SOW (short):
"Redwood bills per token consumed. For pilot participants: sessions with total token consumption below 2,000 tokens are rounded up to the nearest 100-token quantum. Streaming emissions are aggregated at session finalization; chunk-level emissions are not individually rounded. Tokens served entirely from Redwood-managed read-only KV cache (no model execution) will not be billed. A one-time 5,000-token pilot credit and a 10% invoice credit will be applied to the first invoice."

If procurement counters with a fixed dollar floor instead of a rounding rule, propose we accept a prorated floor for month 2 capped at $2,000 for the pilot. Approve this approach?

- Marissa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Alex —

Thanks for the detailed questions. Below are the explicit, billable examples and policies so procurement can review — I formatted them as plain examples rather than legal text.

Billing examples (post-rounding):
- Example A (one-off generation): prompt 250 tokens + response 150 tokens = 400 tokens -> under 2,000 -> rounded up to 400 -> billed 400 tokens (no rounding to 100 boundary since already multiple of 100).
- Example B (chat session): session total 1,120 tokens -> under 2,000 -> nearest 100 quantum -> rounded up to 1,200 tokens billed.
- Example C (embedding-only): single record 64-token input * 10,000 records/day = 640,000 tokens/day -> well above 2,000 so no session-level rounding; billed per-token with standard per-embedding rate.

Streaming behavior:
- We accumulate emitted tokens for the session and apply rounding only once at finalization. Individual stream chunks are not separately rounded. That avoids multiplying rounding by chunk count.

Cache behavior:
- Pure cache hit: the request is served from an immutable, pre-computed vector or prefix without invoking the model runtime -> not billed.
- Cache miss or partial cache + model compute: any token recomputed by the model runtime is billed. We'll provide logs for cache-hit rates on request if you want verification during pilot.

Pilot concessions:
- 10% invoice credit applied to first invoice (applies to billed subtotal after rounding).
- One-time 5,000-token credit to offset small-session rounding inefficiency for early users.
- If usage ramps and you want a guaranteed floor for month 2, we can accept a prorated floor capped at $2,000 for the pilot period.

Next steps:
1) If that all looks good, I'll add the short clause to the SOW and route for signature (DocuSign link below).
2) If procurement wants the fixed-dollar floor instead of the rounding rule, confirm and we'll adjust the SOW language.
